chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad said on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about Allah, the Mighty and High, whether He can be described. He said: 'Do you not read the Qur'an?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you not read His Word, the Mighty and High: (Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends all vision)?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then do you know what vision is know what vision is?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What is it?' I said: 'The vision of the eyes.' He said: 'Verily, the imagination of the hearts is greater than the vision of the eyes. Thus, He is not comprehended by the imagination, and He comprehends the imagination.'
ai.seo_question: Can Allah be described or comprehended by human vision and imagination?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elevates the concept of divine invisibility from mere physical limitation to a fundamental ontological reality, arguing that the 'visions' of the heart (intellectual imagination) are even more limited than physical sight. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of *Tanzih* (transcendence), asserting that Allah’s essence remains utterly incomprehensible to all created faculties, whether sensory or cognitive. The hadith thus refutes any notion that divine attributes can be fully grasped by human intellect, reinforcing the boundary between the Creator and the created.
